newsitem.title: CANADA: Peterson confirmed Canada financial services chief.
newsitem.headline: Peterson confirmed Canada financial services chief.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien confirmed on Wednesday that long-time member of parliament Jim Peterson would become the next junior minister for financial institutions.

The 55-year-old Peterson, formerly head of the House of Commons Finance Committee and first elected in 1980, will be Secretary of State for International Financial Institutions and will work under Finance Minister Paul Martin.
The former secretary of state for financial institutions, Doug Peters, retired at the end of the last parliament.
Canada's big banks and financial institutions will likely be lobbying the new minister to lift a surtax on banks and further deregulate the banking industry.
And foreign bankers will watching to see if the new minister lightens restrictions on foreign investment in the banking sector.
Peterson, who hails from Toronto, the country's financial capital, is brother to former Ontario premier David Peterson.
